title: Otxo
author: Nathan Haddock / Lateralis Heavy Industries & Super Rare Originals
contents: Otxo (pronounced Ot-cho) is a roguelike top-down shooter, taking inspirations from Hotline Miami in graphics, combat and soundtrack. The main difference between the two games is the game loop, with Otxo having randomly generated floors with a hub area for upgrades inbetween and boss fights after beating a certain amount of levels.
Unlike in Hotline, dying is very punishable, forcing you to restart the game from the very beginning. At least the health bar makes the run more forgivable than Hotline Miami's one-shot-death system.

While the game often gets compared to Hotline Miami and gets mentioned plenty of times around the community, its unique features and different game loop offers a new perspective on the 2D top-down shooters genre.
Otxo is available on Steam, PlayStation 4, 5 and the Nintendo Switch.

title: Endless War 1-4
author: Vitaly Zaborov
contents: Endless War is a series of flash games, that you could play in several browser-games websites. It is a top-down shooter, that requires you to reach the end and goal to finish the mission. The path is filled with enemies, that block your way and try to kill you once they spot you. You can either fight back or simply avoid them and reach the goal without hurting anyone.

The games offer a huge variety of settings, including World War 2, the Vietnam War, counter-terrorists, terrorist, the Iraq War and even fictional settings like Fallout, Blood and World War 3 (Humans vs. Aliens).

While the graphics and overall gameplay are comparable to both Hotline Miami and Jonatan's first draft "Super Carnage", there are plenty of features that differ a lot from both Hotline Miami games. For example, Endless War has a weapon arsenal, health and armor as well as grenades. You can also control allies with "Q", offering a more tactical approach on clearing the level. The option to pick up weapons from the ground as well as the presence of cursed bathrooms remain eerily similar to both game series.

Gameplaywise, the series demands more player input, as the enemies remain static most of the time, unless they spot you. Their jank pathfinding and questionable hitboxes make their behavior less predictable than Hotline's, which can result in rather unfair scenarios at times.

Nevertheless the game manages to convey a unique aesthetic and is probably the first exposure to violent top-down shooters for many people at the time, before Hotline Miami came out. You can play the series through "Flashpoint", which serves as a library of flash games, that you can download and play through their program.

title: Inner Animal
author: Jason Cai
contents: A Hotline Miami inspired indie game made in Unity, starring 4 levels for the demo. It offers the same gameplay, with a few slightly changed rules regarding combat, executions and the environment.
The game is available on Jason's Itch.io page at jason-cai.itch.io/inner-animal.

title: Red Hot Vengeance
author: Bros Before Giraffes
contents: Red Hot Vengeance is a twin-stick shooter inspired by Max Payne and Hotline Miami. Its objectives vary from killing every hostile enemy, destroying cargo, to eliminating specific targets. The gunplay is akin to Max Payne 3, as it's heavily gun oriented and lets you use doors, explosive boxes and other objects to your advantage. It also gives you and your enemies a health bar, wich can be refilled with first-aid kits.

Next to the 10 levels of the main story, the game offers a New Game+ mode for extra challenge, as well as 30 unique challenge maps for more variety. It also offers a level editor, which can be then uploaded to the Steam Workshop, much like Hotline Miami 2.

While the story is easy to follow and goes along the typical "Gang War" story arc, its isometric perspective combined with the simplistic art style and use of mainly black, white, grey and red give the game a unique atmosphere.
The game is available on Steam, Itch.io and on Gamejolt.com at no cost.

title: Jackal
author: Transhuman Design
contents: Jackal is a roguelite shooter from an isometric perspective. Set in the 1970s, you and your associate clear out the Mafia in Las Vegas, causing mayhem on the way.

The gameplay can be described as a combination of Hotline Miami's gunplay while adding randomly generated levels, that can be reshuffled by desire, NPCs both hostile and innocent, a stamina bar and a spell system. Spells can be used once per floor, while stamina allows you to either slide or interact with objects by kicking them around.
The game is available on Steam and offers a demo version, that consists of 6 levels, one of them with a bossfight.

title: Kusan: City of Wolves
author: CIRCLEfromDOT & PQube
contents: Kusan is a top-down shooter made in Unity, that is set in the futuristic and anthropomorphic city Kusan, following the story of Mr. Jin and Mr. Ayn. While the gun play, level structure and grade of violence are heavily inspired by Hotline Miami and its sequel, it greatly differs from its art style, environmental details and storytelling.

Both the art direction and environment are much more detailed and varied, as well as interactive either through destructible objects, puzzles or interactions with other creatures, while the story varies in forms of both graphic novels and visual novels.

The player gets a score for each individual floor, which then summarizes the overall performance of the level. The better you are, the more currency you earn, allowing you to unlock perks for its unique inventory / upgrading system. Next to overall improvements to your character, it allows you to focus your play style more on either melee combat, the throwing dagger or ranged weapons.
While the enemies and layout of the levels are less engaging than Hotline Miami's enemy AI, the game makes up for it with its more varied enemy types, bosses and overall details.
You can play a free demo, which includes the first four levels and a final boss and is available on Steam, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S and on the Nintendo Switch.

title: Collect Call
author: Somewhere Else
contents: Your employment has run out. A payphone in the lobby begins to ring. A toneless voice offers vague terms drenched in innuendo. The job pays just twenty-one dollars.

In this gloomy, futuristic dystopia, Collect Call can be best described as "Hotline Miami, but as a card game". It is a turn-based tactical roguelike focused on close quarters combat including a card deck system, trinkets, weapons and disguises. From the various player characters, factions, abilities and secrets, the game offers a wide variety of play styles, card combinations and decisions that affect the story's narrative progression when following the "ascension" route.

It is currently under development with many cards, enemy types and the fundamental game loop and art style already established, with the current plan focusing on adding more player freedom, game modes, playable characters, more enemy factions and finalized art. You can see the most recent developments on their public Discord server at https://discord.gg/Cfn9WtQBNt.

title: Flashes of Chaos
author: Brainburn Studio
contents: The weapon lab has fallen. Chaos reigns inside. Retrieve the lost tech. Infiltrate, survive and escape.

Flashes of Chaos is a roguelike top-down shooter which heavily focuses on modifying you weapons through a vast amount of possible combinations in their abilities and handling. Spreading SMGs? Rapid fire bazookas? Explosive punches? All of that and more are very doable in this game.

The types of levels vary from the basic clear out, to wave based defense to boss levels, that give you special debuffs throughout the level. Enemies vary between gun guys, dogs, suicide bombers and big chainsaw wielding freaks. The more you play, the more perks, weapons and modifiers you get, offering a variety of play styles with each playthrough.
Other than sharing the same perspective and amount of gore, the game vastly differs from Hotline Miami regarding game loop, atmosphere and overall approach at the top-down shooter genre.
Until its non disclosed release date, a public demo is available on Steam.
